acceptance: A test through the MCP stdio server proves not_before="" clears a hold (item ready, take succeeds), also when context is changed in the same call, and that update_item without not_before leaves a hold untouched
The update_item tool description states that not_before="" clears a hold
If an MCP client is found to drop empty strings, the finding is recorded here with the client and version
context:
Imported on 2026-10-28 from the BenchBox tracker item(s): todo-db-update-item-not-before-clear-noop-20261023, todo-db-not-before-clear-and-field-append-20261028. Those items stay open in BenchBox to track the dependency.

In todo-db 0.10.1, store.op_update clears not_before and context when given an empty string (src/todo_db/store.py, op_update), and the changelog documents not_before="" as the way to clear a hold. The reports may therefore come from the MCP client bridge dropping empty strings, or from an older build. Reproduce through todo-db-mcp 0.10.1 on a scratch item before changing code. The append-mode request in the second source item is tracked as update-item-append-mode-and-field-limits.

Source context (todo-db-not-before-clear-and-field-append-20261028): Seen while closing items held until 2026-11-02 after the calendar waits were waived: clearing with an empty string was accepted but the hold stayed. The note-prepend workaround reads then rewrites the whole context field.

REVIEW 2026-10-28 against todo-db 0.10.1 (main d85cdf3), per the todo review checklist and review-protocol L2/L3. VERDICT: NOT REPRODUCIBLE as a server defect; kept for its valid remainder (stdio-level proof and tool text). Repro on a scratch state remote: create_item(not_before='2099-01-01T00:00:00Z') -> take = E_NOTHING_READY; update_item(not_before='') ok, waiting_until absent, ready true; take ok. Same result with context changed in the same call. The two BenchBox items merged here: todo-db-update-item-not-before-clear-noop-20261023 and todo-db-not-before-clear-and-field-append-20261028. The append-mode half of the second is tracked in update-item-append-mode-and-field-limits. Not verified: the omp MCP bridge used in those sessions.

DELIVERED 2026-10-28 through draft PR https://github.com/joeharris76/todo-db/pull/52 (stacked on PR 51; branch feat/update-item-context-append, commit b13ed19; not merged). No server change: the behavior reported did not reproduce. tests/test_mcp_update_semantics.py proves over the MCP stdio protocol that not_before="" clears a hold (item becomes ready and take succeeds), that it does so in the same call as a context change, and that an update which leaves not_before out keeps the hold. The update_item tool description now states that not_before="" clears a hold. The only way to see 'operation produced no state change' is an update that supplies no field, which is what a client produces if it drops an empty-string argument; no MCP client was shown to do so, so acceptance bullet 3 (record the client and version if one drops empty strings) has no finding to record and stays open as an observation, not a blocker. Verification: pytest 276 passed, real stdio smoke on a scratch remote.
description: Two BenchBox reports say update_item with not_before set to an empty string leaves a hold in place and returns E_STATE 'operation produced no state change'. On todo-db 0.10.1 this does not reproduce: through the real todo-db-mcp stdio server, not_before="" clears the hold, the item becomes ready and take succeeds, including when context is changed in the same call. The service layer already has tests (tests/test_not_before.py) but the MCP stdio path does not. The reports match a client that drops empty-string arguments before they reach the server (the symptom 'only context changed' fits that), or an older build.
